profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at dbt Labs
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
I'm a versatile engineer with a knack for writing software that is testable and scalable. I love designing elegant yet simple solutions to complex problems. I also enjoy working on internal tools and processes that make code easier to test and faster to ship. In my most recent role, I was implementing microservices deployed to AWS Lambda, leveraging Kinesis streams, DynamoDB, and ElasticSearch for event management, distributed caching, and data storage. While working in this role over the past few years, I've gained a deep understanding of how to build, test, monitor, and deploy large-scale Serverless applications. Previous to this, I worked at a web-based video company building an expansive automated test suite that encompassed testing streaming protocols, video capabilities, and other front-end features across multiple browsers.

My software toolkit includes:
Languagues: Python, Go, JavaScript, TypeScript
Frameworks: Serverless, gRPC, Django, Flask, ReactTesting Frameworks: RSpec, Capybara, Selenium, Robot Framework, Behave, Cucumber
Load/Performance Test tool: Locust
Databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, ElasticSearch
Methodologies: Object-Oriented Design, Test Driven Development, Agile Development, MVC, REST Version Control: Git, GitHub
Soft Skills: Engineering Empathy, Pair Programming, Team Leadership
Tools for reporting/metrics: Datadog, Looker
Cloud automation tools: Docker, Ansible
AWS technologies: Lambda, Kinesis, Firehose, s3, Glue, Athena, EKS (Kubernetes)

projects.title: Haunted
projects.description:
Haunted is a multiplayer Pac-Man game. It is a mobile responsive app with several game features and a chat room. For the project, we used Firebase API to make the game realtime and used Phaser.js, a JavaScript game development engine, to build game features. 

This project was built over five days with four other members. I specifically worked on game features such as wall collision, winning conditions for players, creating overlap functions for when pacman collides with objects, etc. I also spent a lot of time refactoring our code base. I used namespacing to organize blocks of functionality into easily manageable groups of information. For this, I specifically used object literals to separate our javascript code into separate files (features, game characters, board). It made our code clean and extensible.

projects.title: Senior Thesis
projects.description:
• Analyzed the econometrics underlying financial liberalization in emerging markets to determine its statistical impact on large capital fluctuations and financial crisis
• Used a series of data models to show government easing of directed credit to specific economic sectors, a shift to more flexible interest rates, and easing of entry barriers all increase the chances of observing high current account volatility in emerging markets and increase likelihood of financial crisis
